antonym.name: Opposites
method: Define the word yourself first.
Want the reverse, not just something negative.
One option is a synonym. It is bait.
antonym.example: BRIGHTEN = make lighter, so want DARKEN.

synonym.name: Closest meaning
method: Say it in a phrase you have heard.
Cut the opposite, then the unrelated.
Pick the closest, not the loosely related.
synonym.example: 'A prudent decision' = careful with risk = cautious.

analogy.name: Word pairs
method: Say the link as a short sentence.
Read it back with the third word.
Two fit? Your sentence was too vague.
analogy.example: Pen is the tool a writer uses. Brush, painter.

completion.name: Sentence completion
method: Find the joining word first.
Although, far from = clash. Because, so = agree.
Predict your own word, then match it.
completion.example: 'Because the brief was ___, nobody asked questions.' Predict: clear.

oddword.name: Odd word out
method: Find the group of four, not the odd one.
Usual splits: species vs category, unit vs quantity, verb vs noun.
oddword.example: Sparrow, robin, wren, bird, finch. Four species, one category.

deduction.name: Must-be-true
method: Accept only what is forced.
All A are B puts A inside the bigger B circle.
Inside B does not put you in A.
deduction.example: All surgeons are doctors. Sam is a doctor. Sam may or may not be.

series.name: Number series
method: Write the gaps underneath.
Gaps not constant? Look at the gaps of the gaps.
Growing fast? Try ratios.
Zigzag? Two rules, or two woven sequences.
trick: Check in this order: gaps, gaps-of-gaps, ratios, alternating, squares.
Nine in ten fall to the first two.

percent.name: Percentages
method: Build from 10% and halves.
Successive discounts: one then the other, never added.
Undoing a rise means dividing.
trick: 10% = one decimal place. 5% = half of that. 20% = double it.
Undo a 20% rise: divide by 6, times 5.

pctchange.name: Percentage change
method: Change divided by where you started.
The starting figure is what people get wrong.
Turn it into a fraction you know.

ratio.name: Ratios and sharing
method: Add the parts to get the number of shares.
Divide to find one share.
Multiply up, then check it adds back.
trick: Scale to one unit first. Per-person figures make the rest trivial.

average.name: Averages
method: Average times count gives the total.
Subtract what you know.
Evenly spaced? The middle one is the average.
trick: Average × count = total. That one line solves nearly all of them.
average.example: Four numbers average 20, so total 80. Three make 55, so the fourth is 25.

rate.name: Rates and speed
method: Convert minutes to a fraction of an hour first.
Dividing by a fraction = multiplying by it upside down.
Split awkward multipliers.
trick: ×3.5 means three of it plus half of it.

work.name: Work rate
method: Turn the job into person-hours.
Share that total across the new headcount.
More people means less time. Cross off options first.
trick: Working side by side does not change how long one unit takes.

algebra.name: Simple equations
method: Unknowns one side, numbers the other.
Same operation to both sides.
Substitute back to check.
trick: Five options in front of you: testing beats solving.
Start with the middle value and halve the search.

probability.name: Probability
method: What you want over everything there is.
The bottom is the full total, not the other group.
Simplify, then match the option format.
trick: Always between 0 and 1. Over a half should feel like most of them.

compare.name: Comparing values
method: Put everything in the same form.
Same number of decimal places, then read left to right.

clock.name: Time arithmetic
method: Split into whole hours plus leftover minutes.
Add the hour, then walk up to the next o'clock.
trick: Use the next o'clock as a staging post. It removes the carrying errors.
clock.example: 09:50 + 40 min: 10 gets you to 10:00, then 30 more.

position.name: Counting positions
method: Front plus back equals total plus one.
The plus one is because you count the person twice.
Test any rule on a queue of three.
trick: Front + back = total + 1. Every off-by-one comes from forgetting it.
position.example: Line of 12, 5th from front = 12 − 5 + 1 = 8th from back.

rotation.name: Rotation sequences
method: Pick one landmark and follow only that.
Measure the turn on the first pair, confirm on the second.
Check direction as well as size.
rotation.example: A quarter turn clockwise moves a top landmark to the right.

mirror.name: Mirror or rotation
method: A turn keeps handedness. A flip reverses it.
Ask which side your landmark sits on.
Spin it flat on an imaginary table.
mirror.example: Your two hands are the same shape. No turn makes one into the other.

figanalogy.name: Figure analogies
method: Name the change before looking at the options.
Turned how far, flipped, resized, reshaded.
Apply exactly that to the third figure.
figanalogy.example: First pair turns a quarter clockwise, so the second pair does too.

gridmove.name: Moving grids
method: Separate what moves from what stays.
Treat the shaded square as a dot on a loop.
Corner to edge is one step.
gridmove.example: Top-left to top-middle to top-right is two steps, not one.

gridodd.name: Odd grid out
method: Count first. It often ends the question.
Then spin each grid to line up the block.
The one that never matches is flipped.
gridodd.example: Four Ls in different corners, one mirrored L that never lines up.

countseries.name: Counting sequences
method: Count the thing that changes: sides, dots, lines.
Adding a fixed amount, or multiplying? They diverge fast.
